title: Add gRPC tool-adapter quickstart with schema verifier and contract linting
author: Sofia Alvarez
description: This PR introduces a new quickstart that demonstrates calling external tools over gRPC while enforcing a contract-first approach for RAG/agent responses. Motivation: many enterprise customers run internal services exposed as gRPC and need examples that show how to bind an agent's tool-calling behavior to strongly typed contracts plus runtime verification. The quickstart includes a TypeScript shim, a small Rust gRPC toy-tool implementation (for on-prem friendliness), a JSON Schema-based response verifier that runs as a middleware, and a contract linter that runs in CI to catch schema drift in commits. High-level changes: added quickstart docs, sample code, CI workflows for smoke tests, and a contract linter rule in the repo's linting config. Checklist: - [x] Add TS shim that exposes a tool client compatible with the tool-calling spec - [x] Add Rust example gRPC tool server (echo + structured payloads) - [x] Add JSON Schemas for tool responses and tool call contracts - [x] Add middleware verifier used by the example agent (TS) - [x] Add CI smoke workflow that boots the Rust tool in a container and runs the quickstart smoke runner - [x] Add README with step-by-step local run instructions and expected outputs - [x] Add unit tests for the verifier and linter - [x] Document security notes for on-prem keys and TLS usage Notes: the description in the README demonstrates both streaming and non-streaming tool-call flows, how to wire the schema so the agent can accept only valid tool outputs, and how to configure LLM fallbacks if verifier rejects outputs. This is a self-contained example intended to be copy-paste friendly for customers integrating private gRPC services with Redwood agents.

release_notes: Adds a gRPC tool-adapter quickstart demonstrating contract-first tool calling with a JSON Schema verifier, CI smoke tests, and a contract-linter rule for preventing schema drift.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviewers: security (TLS/key guidance), CI reliability (container startup timeouts), and UX (README run-through). The quickstart is intentionally minimal: replace the Rust sample with any customer gRPC tool implementation and point the TS shim at that endpoint. The verifier middleware is small and designed to be pluggable into Redwood SDKs or user agents.

ci_details: Initial CI run: lint failed (missing license header) — fixed in f6a7b8c. Final CI: all checks passed (unit tests, smoke workflow, contract-linter). Smoke workflow runs the Rust tool in a container, runs the quickstart runner, and uploads the verifier logs as an artifact.
security_review: Security checklist completed: no keys checked in, TLS notes added, KMS guidance included in README, and CI uses ephemeral containers. Recommended follow-ups: include a mTLS example and a note about gRPC reflection being disabled in prod.
how_to_run_local:
1. cd quickstarts/grpc-tool-adapter
2. cargo run --manifest-path rust-tool/Cargo.toml (or use Docker)
3. cd ts-client && npm ci && npm run start:smoke
4. Observe verifier logs and the agent falling back when invalid schema is returned
